newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil shares recoup some losses, 4.99 pct lower.
newsitem.headline: Brazil shares recoup some losses, 4.99 pct lower.

text.p: Brazilian stocks recouped some of Friday's heavy losses in a technical rebound, but were still sharply lower in the early afternoon, brokers said.
The Bovespa index of the 47 most traded stocks were 4.99 percent lower at 11,143 points at 1320 local time/1620 GMT. Total volume was 885.2 million reais ($819.6 million).
Bellwether Telebras preferred, which fell over eight percent earlier, was off 3.7 percent at 141.50 reais.
"The market is bouncing back, but volatility remains," said a senior trader.
Analysts, trying to explain the market's surprising and turbulent volatility this week, said a combination of factors could be pressuring share prices.

Sales from domestic equity funds to cover future withdrawals from retail investors is apparently leading the drop, but sell orders from speculators and banks overbought in stocks are also depressing prices, they said.

"All investors are adjusting their portfolios to a new market risk. Many players were overbought and are now cutting positions while the market seeks new trading levels," said Paulo de Sa Pereira, director at Lloyds Asset Management.

Brazilian shares have provided spectacular gains since the beginning of 1997, particularly driven by domestic mutual funds, which saw new investors, non-traditional players in the bolsa seeking higher yields.

The market's strong run-up was interrupted by profit-taking that most analysts said should be expected, but was intensified early this week by concerns that Brazil could also be affected by speculative moves that forced some Asian nations to devalue.
Those newcomers were the first to take profits.
Asset managers estimate that stock funds lost between 500 million reais and one billion reais this week, but preliminary figures for the week will only be available later in the day.
Last week, total combined stock fund assets were estimated at 19.1 billion reais.

Among other blue chips, state oil firm Petrobras preferred fell 2.05 percent to 287 reais. Private miner Vale do Rio Doce was off 4.78 percent at 25.70 reais, while federal power holding Eletrobras was 5.93 percent lower at 555 reais.
